findings.passage: "It concerns me that every year we're seeing laws passed through this body that make it more difficult to vote despite not having any evidence that there's a problem that we're trying to solve," Sen. Cassie Chambers Armstrong countered.
findings.note: Floor debate on SB 154 (2026): she objects to removing a secondary ID route that about a thousand people used validly in the last cycle. Quoted by WUKY.
subjects: secondary ID with affidavit at the polls

findings.passage: "It's really essential to democracy that everybody have the ability to vote," Chambers Armstrong said.
findings.note: On SB 154 (2026) restricting secondary voter ID forms. Quoted by WKU Public Radio; the same page quotes her adding concern about new laws making voting harder with no evidence of a problem.
subjects: secondary ID with affidavit at the polls

findings.passage: I'm a little worried this is a solution in search of a problem.
findings.note: Committee hearing on the 2024 bill rejecting college-issued student IDs as voter ID (SB 80). She asked whether the Secretary of State or State Board of Elections favoured the change. Quoted by WKMS.

findings.passage: I am still concerned about the data sharing with the federal government — the lack of specificity — this body losing control as we sort of enter into some of those negotiations and concerns around false positives in other states, and making sure that we are not disenfranchising voters through that process,
findings.note: On HB 139 (2026) elections bill, which lets the State Board of Elections share voter rolls with the federal government to identify noncitizens. Date is the article date; the committee remarks were around then. Quoted by WVXU.

findings.passage: “I believe this is already covered, and I worry that we are passing a lot of legislation this session focused on hypothetical problems that might spring up when we have real problems in our communities right now,” Armstrong said.
findings.note: On SB 143 (2024), the constitutional amendment barring noncitizens from voting; she was one of two votes against. Date is the article date. Quoted by The Center Square.
subjects: constitutional amendment on who may vote
